about: What npm run dev -- --fake plays (v5-design §3.10): the fake model’s options (ai/llm/fake-openrouter.ts), this field aside, with KM_AI_FAKE’s on top (hosts/dev/fake.ts). The replies are the GM’s four golden ones (tools/v2/golden-replies.json), one a turn from the opening and round again after the fourth. The notes are the writer’s answer at every call, each on words only one reply has: a know and a why on the opening, two whys on the first reply, a you (when one of the player’s lines shares its words) and a why on the second, a know on the third. Twelve suggested lines (seven to say, two deeds, two risky tries, a way out), so that four are left after every reply once those offered last time and the last three said are screened out, and a way out joins them after four lines. Every model call streams over 2 s (the reply, the stage manager, the notes, the lines); the notes wait 1.5 s more and the lines 0.8 s, so the lines come 2.8 s after the reply, as the prototype’s did live, and the notes 3.5 s after it, once the world has settled: “The GM makes a note…” shows for a moment, and a line can be typed through it. The full GM’s calls (full-gm-design §4.4) answer quietly, so a scene of many lines plays as it does on real models: the memory review’s attention filter flags only what someone witnessed (every other category not flagged), and its memories agent saves one memory for Kell, “What the investigator did” (toolCalls.save_memory); the co-GM finds the scene on track, with a short note and no move of the tracker (the fake’s least JSON would move it back to the first beat); and a considered act (none, unless KM_AI_FAKE’s choices make roll_call new) is ruled a contest with Cob: lifting the folded paper from his boot, Sleight of Hand, guarded, plausible cover, wary: DC 12. Between scenes (story-design §4.4) the hand-off is a plain one that fits any boundary (the golden replies are the yard’s, with their markup), so the notebook’s “how things stood” reads as it would; the verdict is the least JSON (the first scene on, nothing rewritten, no lead), and presence the quiet “here”. KM_AI_FAKE’s choices, byName and toolCalls go beside these, name by name.
replies:
Behind the King’s Granary, a small grey-coated clerk turns slowly from the hoist above the shut loft door. A pigeon watches from the beam. Beneath him, a scrawny boy in a man’s waistcoat and enormous black boots lobs gutter stones upward. “Missed him. Cob’s warming up.” On the wall, a sharp-faced girl swears at him and the morning in Common, then Saltmere dock cant.

A woman in a rain cape steps away from the open gate, notebook in hand. [Sergeant Kell] “Sergeant Agnes Kell. The Captain calls it suicide. I haven’t written that down.” A stone clangs off the hoist hook.

Kell gives a small nod. [Sergeant Kell] “Morning, investigator. Wendell Prout, under-clerk of the Royal Granary Roll. The porters found him at first light. His satchel was empty; I’ve kept it, and his spectacles.” She glances at the stones, pencil poised. “The Captain calls it suicide. I haven’t written that down.”

Cob pauses just long enough to choose a smaller stone. [Cob] “Cob’s helping the dead man spin. He don’t mind.” One stone strikes the cobbles near your boots. “And Cob don’t talk to bluebottles.”[why: You’re beside Sergeant Kell, the watch officer who has caught him twice before.]

The girl on the wall drums her heels. [the girl in the shawl] “He jumped. I saw him. Moonlight and everything.” The sky is still a flat grey after the drizzle.

(Moll’s smirk thins at your question)[you: You told her that from the wall she’d have had her back to the hoist.]. [Moll] “I saw him jump. Didn’t say I saw him climb. You want every bit of it now?”

Kell writes without looking up. [Sergeant Agnes Kell] “Moll says she saw Prout jump at midnight. The rest is not yet stated.” Her pencil pauses.

(Out of character: You can question Kell, Cob or Moll, look closer at the body, the hoist or the barred loft door, or search the yard; if you press someone or try something risky, the dice decide how it goes.)

Kell waits, pencil poised. Out in the lane, a wagon under the wheat-ear canvas of (the Royal Purveyor’s office)[know: The office buys everything the palace eats and burns, by the King’s old right; its wheat-ear is on every palace wagon in the street.] rumbles past the gate.

ruling.act: lift the folded paper from the boy’s boot
ruling.reason: to lift the folded paper from the boy’s boot without him noticing

success.happens: While the boy watches the sergeant, your fingers find the folded paper at the top of his boot and it comes away. He doesn’t feel a thing.
establishes: The investigator has the folded paper from the boy’s boot.

failure.happens: The boy jerks his foot away and backs off to the wall, glaring. “Hands off! Cob knows your sort.” The paper stays in his boot, and he keeps the sergeant between you.
establishes: The boy caught the investigator reaching for his boot.

args.title: What the investigator did
args.context: In the granary yard, the morning Wendell Prout was found hanged, with the investigator the King lent me.
args.content: I watched what the King’s investigator did in the yard, close enough to swear to it. I wrote it down. If anyone asks, I can say what I saw.

suggestions:
say: Sergeant, who found him, and when?
say: Cob, that's a good arm. Were you about here last night?
do: (I look up at the loft door above the hoist)
try: (I try to win the boy over with a friendly word and a coin, to hear what he saw)
say: Who's the girl on the wall?
say: Was the loft door shut like that when he was found?
do: (I walk once round the yard, looking at the ground under the hoist)
try: (I try to read the girl while Cob throws, to see if she's hiding something)
leave: (I tell Kell I've seen enough for now and head back to the palace)
say: Sergeant, why haven't you written it down?
say: Has anyone been up to the loft since he was found?
say: Did anyone hear anything in the night?
handoff:
The scene ended as it was played, and Sergeant Kell has it all in her notebook.
- Kell was beside the investigator throughout: she saw and heard everything they did, and can swear to it.
- Nothing changed hands that isn't written down.
- Kell goes on with the investigator.
